verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः
verse.line: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.
verse.translation: Like a torch of tinduka wood, blaze, even if only for a moment. Do not smoulder without flame like a fire of husks, just to stay alive.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: About wholehearted effort, not reckless risk or burnout.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to Rama while he is weighed down by sorrow. The young prince has lost his kingdom and feels the future is closed. Vasishtha tells him that the fruit of action comes from effort itself. The timing of that fruit, whether it arrives early or late, is what people call fate. He explains that your past effort made today what it is, and your present effort will make tomorrow. Do not grieve for what was never in your hands to control.
verse.for_you: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari addresses the reader from a section on steadfastness. He says let people praise or blame you. Let money come or go. Let death come today or ages from now. The steady person does not step off the right path. Setbacks do not last long for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.for_you: The days of your new work will be hard and the money will not be there yet. Let the praise or blame come. Let the money come or go. The only thing that matters is that you do not step off the path you chose. Keep going.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: In the forest, Draupadi tells Yudhishthira that waiting for fate is no strategy. She says that crying over unrewarded effort is useless. Every attempt can end in success or failure, and only by refusing to act is the outcome guaranteed. She is saying that you could act, because the only way to fail for sure is to stop trying.
verse.for_you: The fire you feel is not a feeling to wait for. It is a choice to keep working while the money is not there. Do the next small thing for the work itself, not for the reward that has not arrived.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna tells Arjuna to act fully but let go of owning the result. Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the outcome be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing. Care, plan, and aim well, but do not let the result own you.
verse.for_you: You cannot control the money that comes or goes. You can only control the next small thing you do today. Do that one thing fully, and let go of needing it to prove anything right now.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.for_you: The fire you feel is not in the results. It is in the steady act of doing what you have chosen. Today, keep your promise to your brand by doing one small thing that moves it forward, without waiting for the feeling to return first.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

prasang.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
prasang.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

story.for_you: Hanuman’s resolve survived the first hard morning because it was tied to a promise, not a feeling. Your brand will survive the hard days the same way, by keeping your promise to your work even when the leap feels too long.

script: You left your job just last week and now the days feel huge. The money is not there. You told me you are more alive than ever, but you are afraid the feeling will go out.
Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying on the ground. He has lost his kingdom and he has given up. She sees him smouldering in despair and she will not let him stay there. And Vidula replies:
अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः.
In plain words: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.

A flame that burns without a flame is just smoke. It looks like fire but it gives no heat. Vidula is telling her son that a life without a blaze is a life without power. She wants him to burn bright, even for a moment. This is easier said than done, because the fear of losing it is real, but a torch does not last forever. It is meant to burn.
Let the fear be there. Let it sit beside you. But do not wait for the feeling to come back to you. Start the work while the fear is there. Let it be the wind under the flame.
What is one small thing you can do today that makes you burn?

depth.practice: When the fear comes, do not wait for the feeling to return. Do one small thing for the brand right then.
